finding.claim: deleteAccount calls canDelete() but ignores the boolean result (it should call assertCanDelete()). The authorization check is a no-op, so any user can delete any account by id. This is a broken access control / IDOR bug.
finding.source: Any authenticated user sends DELETE /accounts/{id} with an arbitrary account id. The user is not the owner and not an admin.
finding.sink: accounts.remove(id) at AccountService.java:23, which deletes the account.

trace.note: deleteAccount(User u, long id) is the handler for DELETE /accounts/{id}; id is attacker-controlled
Account is looked up by id with no ownership filter
canDelete(u, a) returns false for a non-owner non-admin, but the return value is discarded, so execution continues

finding.guards_checked: canDelete (line 9-11) computes the right policy but is only advisory here. No exception is thrown and there is no other guard in this file. The sibling closeAccount correctly uses assertCanDelete (line 29), which confirms the intended control was missed in deleteAccount. No caller-side or framework-level check is visible in the repo, which contains only this file.

verdict.guard_found: canDelete (AccountService.java:9-11) returns a boolean and does not throw. assertCanDelete (13-17) throws SecurityException but is not called in deleteAccount. No other guard exists in the repo, which contains only this file.
verdict.reason: AccountService.java:22 calls canDelete(u, a) as a bare statement and discards the boolean, so accounts.remove(id) at line 23 runs for any user. closeAccount at line 29 correctly uses assertCanDelete. An authenticated non-owner, non-admin user can therefore delete any account.

verdict_facts.guard_found: canDelete (AccountService.java:9-11) returns a boolean but its result is discarded at line 22; assertCanDelete (13-17) would throw but is not called in deleteAccount. No other guard in the file.
verdict_facts.reason: AccountService.java:22 calls canDelete(u, a) as a bare statement, discarding the boolean, so accounts.remove(id) at line 23 runs for any authenticated user, owner or not (unlike closeAccount at line 29, which uses assertCanDelete).
